title: Polarization Around the Character of 'Ali — Glossary

entries.gloss: The book's governing category: the forces by which people are drawn toward or pushed away from one another in social and moral life.
Contrariety or opposition; Mutahhari presents resemblance and contrariety as basic causes of human attraction and repulsion.
The school of devotion to 'Ali as presented by Mutahhari, whose spirit he connects with discernment of truth and principled attraction and repulsion.
Love and mercy: the higher human sentiment contrasted with merely possessive or passionate love.
A transformative force whose moral effect depends on its object and the way the lover responds to it.
The limiting defensive structure of the ego; the book's discipline is to expand the self's concern rather than simply despise the self.
The movement that emerged from the Siffin arbitration crisis and developed a rigid religious-political doctrine that Mutahhari treats as a recurring spirit as well as a historical sect.
The people of Jamal whom 'Ali described as those who broke their allegiance.
The people of Siffin whom 'Ali described as those who deviated from the path.
The Khawarij of Nahrawan, described as those who passed beyond or missed the truth of the religion.
The arbitration at Siffin that became the immediate setting for the emergence of the Khawarij.
Bidding to good and forbidding evil; the book stresses that it requires knowledge and sound judgment about effective action and consequences.
Dissimulation discussed in the historical treatment of the Khawarij and the reasons their inflexibility contributed to their decline.
A form of outward conformity masking an opposing inner commitment; the book contrasts it with principled love that remains aligned with truth.
The unusually broad tolerance 'Ali extended to the Khawarij while they remained within the sphere of criticism and speech, before armed revolt changed the situation.
